summary: 1929 L-2 cupola cabin on Priscilla Peak, Lolo National Forest, Montana; rental program withdrawn; 2020 move-to-Driveway-Peak plan cancelled.

facts.design: L-2 cupola cabin with shake walls and gable roof (a cabin, not a tower)
facts.status_note: Still on the summit per the 2020 Ledger article, which says it has fallen into disrepair.

visit.trail_note: Trailhead not clearly signed, per NHLR visit report; no NHLR sign posted at the trailhead or on the directions.

corrections.why: The NHLR describes a 1929 cupola cabin with no tower height; no source gives 91.4 m (about 300 ft), so the figure looks like a data error.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR visit form answers Sometimes to Staffed?, while firelookout.com says the cabin was used for emergencies into the 1970s. Recorded the emergency-use history as the staffing fact; current staffing is not established by any source read.

The 2020 Ledger article and the Forest Service page describe a proposed move to Driveway Peak. The Forest Service page lists that project as Cancelled, so the record keeps the cabin on Priscilla Peak and treats the move as a cancelled proposal, not a relocation.

notes_for_editor: Core build and registry facts are solid (NHLR). Historical staffing comes from newspaper clippings transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page; originals not checked, and personal details in those clippings (a 1955 accident, a 1956 medical evacuation) were left out on purpose. The 2006 visit report is the latest condition record found; no 2020s condition or access source was found. The record's 91.4 m height looks wrong for a cabin and is proposed for removal. Public access is not confirmed by any source read, so no access level is set. The Forest Service project page was last updated 2020-06-17. NHLR id=892 page, a different URL, was not needed.
